summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea lasting four days, with concern for infectious colitis. A CT scan showed colonic wall thickening consistent with focal colitis, and she was treated empirically with antibiotics. She also experienced transient chest pain, but cardiac workup showed no acute ischemia. A non-healing sternal wound from prior CABG was debrided, and a wound vac was placed; oral Augmentin was started for prophylaxis. Hypernatremia and lactic acidosis from dehydration improved with IV fluids. Her heart failure was managed cautiously without diuresis due to acute kidney injury, and her blood pressure was controlled with IV then oral medications. She regained oral intake, symptoms resolved, and she was discharged back to extended care with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
